decisions.decision: Keep `due` as an optional field in the version 1 data file, accepting that 1.4.0 can read every ticket but can erase saved deadlines the next time it writes the file.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect a rollback that accepts new writes and still retains the exact deadlines already assigned when the upgraded release returns.

decisions.decision: Have operators stop the service that writes the production file, run a separate offline backfill command against that file, and then start the service with deadlines enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect the release to backfill automatically while running with deadlines hidden, so operators can enable them after completion without a separate offline migration.
decisions.where: record/03-research.md:13 (summary), record/06-plan.md:89–102 (switchover and concurrency), and record/08-step-plan-W1.md:149 (S1 proof invokes the command with DATA_FILE).

decisions.decision: On enabled startup, exit before listening and report missing deadlines if any ticket in the persistent file still needs backfill.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect an early activation attempt to leave the API serving legacy responses while alerting operators that deadlines are still disabled.

decisions.decision: Assign new tickets a saved deadline at creation even with the switch off, using the switch to gate ticket output and overdue filtering.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect tickets created during the disabled period to remain without deadlines until the pre-activation backfill assigns them under the rollout policy.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–10 (R-1 through R-3) and record/06-plan.md:60–76 (API and state concerns).

decisions.decision: Use each legacy ticket's saved priority at migration time, even if the ticket was created at a different priority.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect backfill to use the ticket's priority at creation, recovered from its history.

decisions.decision: Use the response-time settings in effect when the backfill command runs to assign missing deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect the original four response-time defaults to govern the backlog and configuration overrides to apply only to newly created tickets.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–12 (R-1 and R-4) and record/09-test-spec-W1.md:26 (TC-2 changes config on retry).

decisions.decision: Count response-time hours as continuous elapsed time, including nights and weekends.
decisions.alternative: The requester might mean hours when the help desk is staffed, with the countdown paused outside that schedule.

decisions.decision: Make response times optional, validated per-priority environment settings supplied to the process.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect help-desk leads to update a saved policy while the service is running without asking an operator to change the process environment.

decisions.decision: Fill missing deadlines in one atomic write, preserve other logical data, and have a retry leave previously assigned deadlines in place even after the settings change.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect operators to be able to correct a backfill run with the wrong settings before activation by rerunning it with the intended policy.

decisions.decision: Intersect the overdue set with the existing status-or-priority match set, even though the current API guide describes status and priority as cumulative filters.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect a query specifying overdue, status, and priority to return only tickets satisfying all three conditions, as the API guide's filter rule suggests.

decisions.decision: Leave audit entries and notification payloads as they are, including when deadlines are assigned.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect deadline assignment to appear in ticket history or the receipt notification so agents or requesters can see the original promise.
decisions.where: record/06-plan.md:65–69 (messaging concern) and repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:7–12 (R-2 and R-4).

decisions.decision: Show deadlines in human-readable CLI list and show output when enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might intend the new field for API responses and expect existing command-line output to stay the same even after activation.

decisions.decision: Keep the four raw list columns and the weekly report free of deadline data even when deadlines are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect a machine-readable CLI view with deadlines that scripts can explicitly select while existing consumers keep their four columns.

decisions.decision: Expose `due` in enabled API responses that return tickets, including responses to ticket writes.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect deadlines on ticket reads and lists while existing create, update, and transition clients keep their original response shape.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:7–8 (R-2) and record/09-test-spec-W1.md:17–21 (TC-1 includes an enabled create response).

decisions.decision: Apply the overdue condition before cursor pagination, so pages and next cursors are built from matching tickets.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect overdue to narrow each existing page while keeping its position and next cursor in the unfiltered list.

decisions.decision: Expose `due` in ticket API responses as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect a timestamp carrying the help desk's local time-zone offset so the deadline can be read directly in local time.

decisions.decision: Recognize only the exact query value `overdue=true` as activating the filter when deadlines are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect a validated Boolean parameter that returns a client error for malformed values instead of leaving the overdue filter inactive.

decisions.decision: Treat a ticket as overdue only after its due timestamp is strictly earlier than the request clock.
decisions.alternative: The requester might expect a ticket to start appearing in overdue results the instant its deadline is reached.
